request: Expand more existing major timeline events as full readable quest histories; continue prioritizing Interregional/World Changing entries and leave Alavara aside.

scope.reading: The three bounded quest sequences and selected memorial/Crucible antecedents are reviewed, with closing rulings and proper reply context. Source discovery, copied working windows and exact ID/hash checks are distinct from exhaustive reading of every cached message. Earlier qualified funeral and later civic background retain their existing public-reference limits.
scope.excluded: No raw transcripts, controller identities, private laboratory procedures, intimate material, unreviewed attachments, protected lore or new character/location identity is imported.

decisions: All three already-listed Interregional milestones keep their routes, dates, importance, regions and calendar adjustments. No new event or record is created. Three summaries gain specific action; the related existing duel summary changes only banishment to the source’s exile.

Aelthor includes preparation, Verdant Circle lightning, field commands, wave attacks, the loss of Scribonia’s simulacrum, Eugene’s contaminated attack, attempts at banishment, the temporal incarnate, Elenia’s healing of Olokun, the uncast Meteor Swarm, the final blow, care for the fallen and Aria’s speech. The staff Beacon of Hope is not confused with a same-named spell.

Eugene falls, Scribonia believes him dead, and he later wakes while Elenia calls him unconscious. The sequence establishes his awakening but does not establish an exact resurrection spell. Nor does a plan to restore other soldiers prove every attempt succeeded. Casualties remain hundreds or perhaps thousands, not a fabricated exact roll.

Aria’s and Scribonia’s explanations of the attack remain attributed; neither a secret acquisition nor a universal divine motive is made public fact. Her field authority/acclaim do not replace Zarathis’s civic institutions or prove unanimous support.

The council includes seating/protocol, Forbiddance affecting Jiangshi’s ancestors, uncertain travel/scouting, Adelia’s absent consent, faction offers, Magnus’s ordinary mirror, the proposed pact and its rejection, and continued war preparations. An attendant, not Jiangshi herself, collects the clothing/bones. Arandiel’s prior erroneous masculine pronoun is corrected against the explicit quest context.

The mirror is ordinary after Míriel tests it; Magnus’s hopes and restoration claims do not prove a working transport or artifact recipe. Private laboratory details and raw procedures are omitted. Gate travel requires a known destination in this discussion; no universal travel rule is invented.

Bowene’s rejection replies directly to Olokun’s plea against a pact with Death. It does not end all war preparations. The ending retains his order to stop arguing, his future orders and Scribonia’s qualified offer to navigate.

Exile’s antecedents distinguish the 99 returned soldiers from those taken by Death: Elenia clarifies they are Aionia’s dead. The sanctioned duel, narrator-reported fall/death, subsequent life/healing and contested ethics do not establish a named resurrection spell or turn Adelia’s attempted-murder accusation into an agreed legal ruling.

Only Elenia’s departure is required in the judgment. Aravil and Olokun’s solidarity, the invitation to others, material aid, sending stone and possibility of future law reform remain distinct from a permanent universal ban or automatic right to return. The new setting distinguishes the hearing below Ciaránach from departure at the Shining Shores and the Babel destination.

Adelia supports banishment and later offers aid; Elenia does not accept an immediate reconciliation. Magnus’s promise of Silver Star acceptance is a claim, not completed membership. Proposed companions are not a confirmed roster, and no unrecorded crossing is invented.
